Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, on Wednesday received the country’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, following their historic triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Mrs Tinubu received the players on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, alongside Nana Shettima, the wife of Vice-President Kashim Shettima, and other government officials. During the reception, the First Lady presented bouquets of flowers to the players in celebration of their achievement. The Flamingos made history on Saturday after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final played in Rabat, Morocco, to become the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring in the 39th minute before Oluebube Umejiaku doubled Nigeria’s lead shortly after the restart. Japan scored a late goal through Fuki Ito, but the Nigerian side held on to secure the historic victory. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. In a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, the President praised the players for their courage, discipline and determination. “What wonderful news to return home to! Our young girls have conquered the world and given Nigerians everywhere another reason to celebrate our great country,” he said. He particularly commended Bashiru and Umejiaku for their goals, adding that the players had written their names in gold. APC women mobilise support for Tinubu in Jigawa Flamingos: Omokri accuses Obi of politicising victory Senate splashes N100m on Flamingos Similarly, Mrs Tinubu congratulated the team, describing their triumph as a demonstration of resilience, teamwork and commitment. She noted that the players had overcome a shaky start to win six consecutive matches and lift the trophy. “Through your team spirit, dedication and hard work, Nigeria is again the toast of the world,” the First Lady said. The reception on Wednesday was another recognition of the team’s achievement, which has been widely celebrated across the country.
